claims.content: At the main_flow point where a bid is about to be allowed (main_flow should include a bidder sign-in status check before bid placement; if this step is not yet present, it must be added), if the bidder has not signed in, the system does not place the bid and instead takes the bidder directly to the sign-in page. Exit: continue to exception step 2.

After the bidder signs in, if the bidder has the required minimum information to bid, the system returns the bidder to the product details page of the item they initially tried to bid on. If the bidder lacks the required minimum information, the bid is not placed and the exception flow terminates without returning to bid placement. Exit: return to the main_flow step where the bidder views the product details page and can re-attempt placing the bid (when requirements are satisfied); otherwise the use case ends.
Customer
The bidder is signed in.
The bidder has the required minimum information to bid.
The Customer's bid is successfully placed, and the system records the bid amount and bid type in the Item Bid History, displaying the bidder's name, amount, date placed, and bid status.
After confirming the bid, the Customer remains on the product details page.
The Customer views the Product Details Page for the auction item, which displays current bid information and bidding input fields.
The Customer selects one of the supported bid methods and, where applicable, enters the bid amount in the corresponding field.
The Customer initiates the bid by clicking the button corresponding to the selected method (e.g., 'Place SmartBid').
The system verifies that the Customer is signed in and has the required minimum information to bid; the verification succeeds.
The system displays a Bid Confirmation Popup asking the Customer to verify the bid amount, bid type, and payment method details.
The Customer confirms the bid by clicking the 'Yes, Place SmartBid' (or equivalent) button in the confirmation popup.
The system records the bid amount and bid type in the Item Bid History, displaying the bidder's name, amount, date placed, and bid status.

The Customer, while viewing the Product Details Page for an auction item, clicks either the 'QuickBid Now' button for a single increment bid or the 'Place SmartBid' / 'Place Single Bid' button after entering a desired bid amount.
The Customer places a bid on an auction item using one of the supported bid methods (QuickBid Now, SmartBid, or Single Bid).

scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has confirmed the bid and the bid has been placed/recorded for that auction item.

Main Flow step 1 then restarts at 'Customer views the Product Details Page', and steps 2-3 repeat the same method selection, amount entry, and bid initiation that the Trigger already completed, causing an overlap instead of starting where the Trigger left off. (slot already rewritten once; further slot_rewrite suppressed)

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger ends with the Customer clicking a bid button (after optionally entering a bid amount), but Main Flow step 1 restarts with the Customer viewing the Product Details Page, and steps 2-3 repeat the Trigger's method selection/amount entry/button click. Thus Main Flow does not pick up where the Trigger left off.

inconsistency_hints: [slot_rewrite] The Trigger ends with the Customer clicking a bid button, but the Main Flow step 1 starts with the Customer viewing the Product Details Page and step 3 repeats the same bid-button click. The Main Flow thus restarts before the Trigger instead of picking up where it left off.

Alternative flow claim 3 says 'Diverges from Step 6' but restates the exact behavior already in main_flow step 6 (confirming via 'Yes, Place SmartBid' or equivalent); it is not a genuine alternative branch.

Exception flow step 2 only defines an exit for the case where the bidder has the required minimum information after signing in; if the bidder lacks that information, the branch has no clear exit (no return to main_flow, termination, or handoff).
